tweet_summary: Middle East Observer (376K followers) posts an 'unconfirmed initial report' from 'Iranian witness channels' that a US F-15 was shot down by Iran and police went to capture the pilot — telling readers to 'stay tuned for confirmation.'
why_note_decision: Even though the author hedges with 'unconfirmed,' the tweet circulates a specific factual claim (US F-15 shot down by Iran, pilot captured) that mainstream sources directly contradict: on March 1 2026, CENTCOM confirmed three US F-15Es were downed by Kuwaiti friendly fire (not by Iran), and all six aircrew ejected safely and were recovered. The 'Iranian witness channel' framing is exactly the kind of rumor-laundering that benefits from a corrective note before it spreads further. The original note correctly cited CENTCOM and was structurally sound; raters tagged 'note not needed' partly because the post was small (12 ratings, modest visibility) and partly because the author had already hedged. We still think a note is warranted given the specificity of the false sub-claim and Iran-war info-environment stakes.
judge_guidance: A correct note must (1) state that CENTCOM confirmed the F-15E losses were caused by Kuwaiti friendly fire, not Iranian action, (2) state that all six aircrew ejected safely and were recovered — no US pilot was captured by Iran, (3) cite the CENTCOM press release (centcom.mil) or a wire/major outlet (Stars and Stripes, Military Times, Reuters/AP) as the source. MUST NOT: (a) speculate beyond the public record, (b) editorialize about Iran's motives, or (c) cite only social-media or partisan sources. PASS if the note clearly contradicts the 'shot down by Iran / pilot captured' framing using CENTCOM, in under ~280 chars. FAIL if it merely says 'unconfirmed' without naming the friendly-fire correction or omits the 'all crew safe' part.
reference_note: US CENTCOM confirmed three US F-15Es were downed by Kuwaiti air defenses in a friendly-fire incident on Mar 1, 2026; all six aircrew ejected and were recovered. No US aircraft was shot down by Iran and no pilot was captured. https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PRESS-RELEASES/Press-Release-View/Article/4418568/three-us-f-15s-involved-in-friendly-fire-incident-in-kuwait-pilots-safe

original_unhelpful_note.text: Unverified Iranian claims of an F-15 shootdown and pilot capture contradict US CENTCOM: three US F-15s were downed by Kuwaiti air defences in Kuwait in a friendly-fire incident and all pilots ejected and were recovered. https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PRESS-RELEASES/Press-Release-View/Article/4418568/three-us-f-15s-involved-in-friendly-fire-incident-in-kuwait-pilots-safe
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Note is largely correct, but raters lean 'note not needed' on a low-volume hedged rumor post. Borderline rater fatigue; the correction itself is accurate and useful.

fact_check.claim_verdict: false — the F-15E losses were Kuwaiti friendly-fire, not Iranian shootdowns, and no pilots were captured
fact_check.notes: CENTCOM confirmed three F-15Es lost on Mar 1 2026 to Kuwaiti air defenses during combat against Iran; all six crew safe. Iranian channels claiming an Iran-credited shootdown + pilot capture are not supported.

importance.lens_rationale: Active US-Iran war infosphere; correcting bogus shootdown/pilot-capture rumors matters for escalation dynamics and is relevant to global-security/EA priorities.
